body: Could you test the reproducer with `resteasy-reactive-qute` as well?

So the difference between `@Inject Template basic` and `@Location("basic.html") Template located` is that for the first one the template path is "incomplete" and the actual template is _selected_ in the `io.quarkus.resteasy.qute.runtime.TemplateResponseFilter` right before the rendering (based on accept headers). For `@Location("basic.html")` the path is "complete" and the `TemplateResponseFilter` does not set the media type explicitly.
@mkouba with `quarkus-resteasy-qute`replaced with `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` in pom.xml, both endpoints return `Content-Type=text/html;charset=UTF-8`.
In RESTEasy Reactive we explicitly add the charset when it makes sense. I have no idea why there is a difference in RESTEasy Classic.
@fedinskiy Is `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` a viable solution to your problem?

@mkouba my "problem" was to test `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` and `quarkus-resteasy-qute`  :)

As I mentioned earlier, this behaviour doesn't happen when `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` is used.

> As I mentioned earlier, this behaviour doesn't happen when `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` is used.

Yes, I know. My question is whether switching to `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` is an option?

Option for who?

We (Quarkus QE team) have coverage for both classic[1] and reactive[2] scenarios and will keep it for foreseeable future anyway. This quirk does not stop us from performing other tests, so it is not a problem for us.
I can not predict, if it will be a problem for other users, and whether they can switch from regular `quarkus-resteasy-qute` to `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` to solve it.

[1] https://github.com/quarkus-qe/quarkus-test-suite/blob/main/qute/synchronous/src/test/java/io/quarkus/ts/qute/QuteIT.java#L33
[2] https://github.com/quarkus-qe/quarkus-test-suite/blob/main/qute/reactive/src/test/java/io/quarkus/ts/qute/QuteReactiveIT.java#L33

> Option for who?
>

This quirk does not stop us from performing other tests, so it is not a problem for us. I can not predict, if it will be a problem for other users, and whether they can switch from regular `quarkus-resteasy-qute` to `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-qute` to solve it.
> 
> [1] https://github.com/quarkus-qe/quarkus-test-suite/blob/main/qute/synchronous/src/test/java/io/quarkus/ts/qute/QuteIT.java#L33 [2] https://github.com/quarkus-qe/quarkus-test-suite/blob/main/qute/reactive/src/test/java/io/quarkus/ts/qute/QuteReactiveIT.java#L33

Ok, I forgot that you're from the Quarkus QE team and the description did not mention this. So I thought that it's a problem of a user ;-).

In any case, I have no idea how to fix this in `resteasy-classic` and as I mentioned in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27872#issuecomment-1243786296 - it's expected from the qute point of view.
